summary.title: Main Page
summary.one_liner: The Chess Programming Wiki is a hierarchical reference covering every aspect of programming computers to play chess, from basics like search and evaluation to engines, people, and tools.
takeaways: CPW is a reference wiki for computer chess programming, organized hierarchically through a left-hand navigation bar.
Getting Started and basic topics include board representation, search, evaluation, opening books and endgame tablebases.
The wiki covers bitboard techniques such as magic bitboards and different ways to implement LMR.
The site includes lists of engines (including the CPW-Engine), software, hardware, people, organizations, and tournaments.
CPW was founded by Mark Lefler in 2007 and moved hosts after Wikispaces closed; the page says lichess.org offered to take over hosting on August 3, 2026.
summary.summary: This is the main page of the Chess Programming Wiki, a reference for programming computers to play chess. It describes the wiki's structure: a left-hand navigation bar, hot topics, basics such as search, evaluation and opening books, and lists of engines, software, people and tournaments. It also gives a short history of the site, founded by Mark Lefler in 2007 and moved after the Wikispaces closure. The page itself is an index, so it points to other articles rather than explaining techniques in depth.
